# Cognition configuration (`cognition.toml`)

This page describes the operator's cognition configuration as this build reads it. Every key, type, bound
and default comes from the Pydantic models in `cognition/lm-controller/src/mineworld_cognition/config.py`.
Rules a schema cannot express, such as which `kind` accepts which option, are written in the description of
the field they belong to, and the loader enforces them.

The file belongs to you, never to a world. The package README is
[`cognition/lm-controller/README.md`](../../cognition/lm-controller/README.md). The machine-readable schema is
[`schema/cognition-toml.schema.json`](schema/cognition-toml.schema.json).

A key marked *Required* must be present. A key marked *unset* may be left out and has no value. Keys that are
not listed here are refused by the loader.

## `[recording]`

The `[recording]` table: where answers come from, and whether they are recorded.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | one of `live`, `record`, `replay`, `scripted` | yes | none | none | Where answers come from. `live`: the configured backend answers. `record`: the backend answers and each answer is written to the cassette. `replay`: answers are read from the cassette, and no network client is built. `scripted`: a backend supplied in code, for tests. |
| `cassette` | text, or unset | no | unset | none | The cassette file, which `record` writes and `replay` reads. Required for `record` and `replay`. A relative path is resolved against this configuration file. |

## `[tiers]`

The `[tiers]` table: which backend answers each decision tier. Keys are tier names (`ordinary_decision`, `social`, `major_decision`, `summarize`; their meaning is in ARCHITECTURE.md §9.1). Values are a backend name from `[backends.<name>]`, or `none` for a tier that uses no model. A tier left out uses no model, the same as `none`.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ordinary_decision` | text: a backend name, or `none` | no | unset | none | The backend that answers this tier. |
| `social` | text: a backend name, or `none` | no | unset | none | The backend that answers this tier. |
| `major_decision` | text: a backend name, or `none` | no | unset | none | The backend that answers this tier. |
| `summarize` | text: a backend name, or `none` | no | unset | none | The backend that answers this tier. |

## `[budgets]`

The `[budgets]` table: the limits of `BudgetPolicy`, and where the spend is kept.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `calls_per_wall_hour` | whole number | no | `20` | >= 1 | The most model calls one person's seat may make in any rolling hour of real time. Real time is wall-clock seconds, not simulated days. |
| `tokens_per_wall_day` | whole number | no | `30000` | >= 1 | The most tokens one seat may use in any rolling 24 hours of real time. |
| `max_in_flight` | whole number | no | `2` | >= 1 | The most model calls that may run at the same time in this process. |
| `call_timeout_s` | whole number | no | `20` | >= 1 | Seconds to wait for one model call before it is abandoned. |
| `ledger` | text, or unset | no | unset | none | A SQLite file that keeps the spend, so a restart neither resets it nor counts a call twice. Unset keeps the spend in memory only. A relative path is resolved against this configuration file. |

## `[backends.<name>]`

The `[backends.<name>]` tables: one per backend, named by you. A name uses lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, and does not start or end with `-` or `_`.

`<name>` must match the pattern `^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9_-]*[a-z0-9])?$`. One table per backend:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | one of `openai-compatible`, `anthropic` | no | `"openai-compatible"` | none | `openai-compatible` for a server that speaks the OpenAI chat API: a local server or a hosted provider. `anthropic` for Claude, through Anthropic's Messages API. |
| `preset` | one of `openai`, `xai`, `deepseek`, `glm`, `zai`, `mistral`, `moonshot`, `dashscope`, `gemini`, `openrouter`, `groq`, or unset | no | unset | none | A named hosted provider. It fills `base_url`, `key_env`, `structured_output` and `temperature` when this table leaves them out. Not allowed with `kind = "anthropic"`. |
| `base_url` | text | yes | none | none | The address of the server, for example `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` for a local server. Required unless `preset` supplies it. Use `https` unless the host is a loopback address. It must not carry a user name, a password, a query or a fragment. |
| `model` | text | yes | none | length >= 1, length <= 200 | The model name the server expects, for example `qwen3.5:4b`. |
| `key_env` | text | no | `""` | none | The NAME of the environment variable that holds the API key, for example `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`: upper-case letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. Empty when the server needs no key. A preset fills it when this table leaves it out. The key itself is never written in this file. |
| `structured_output` | one of `json_schema`, `json_object`, `none` | no | `"json_schema"` | none | How the server is asked for structured output. `json_schema`: the server enforces the output schema. `json_object`: the server returns any JSON object, and MineWorld checks it against the schema. `none`: no structured-output request is sent. |
| `reasoning` | one of `unset`, `off`, `low`, `medium`, `high` | no | `"unset"` | none | The reasoning effort the server should use: `off`, `low`, `medium` or `high`. `unset` sends no reasoning setting. Not allowed with `kind = "anthropic"`. |
| `temperature` | one of `send`, `omit` | no | `"send"` | none | `send` sends the sampling temperature with each request. `omit` leaves it out, for a model that refuses a temperature. |
| `request_timeout_s` | whole number, or unset | no | unset | >= 1, <= 3600 | Seconds to wait for one answer from this backend, from 1 to 3600. Unset means this table sets no request timeout. |
| `retry` | see the description, or unset | no | unset | none | The `[backends.<name>.retry.<layer>]` tables: retry layers for the seats that use this backend, between a seat's own override and `[retry]`. |

## `[secrets]`

The `[secrets]` table: an optional `.env`-style file that holds API keys.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env_file` | text, or unset | no | unset | none | A `.env`-style file that holds API keys, read only when named here. A relative path is resolved against this configuration file. On macOS and Linux the file must not be readable by its group or by others (`chmod 600`); the loader refuses it otherwise. |

## `[controller]`

The `[controller]` table: the consult's bounds and the seat's timing (pr-s10-p6 §5.13).

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `consult_deadline_s` | whole number | no | `20` | >= 1, <= 120 | Wall seconds from a trigger's receipt to the submit, from 1 to 120. |
| `max_calls` | whole number | no | `5` | >= 1, <= 10 | The most model calls one consult may make, from 1 to 10. |
| `handback_s` | whole number | no | `10` | >= 1, <= 600 | Wall seconds a seat stays with its fallback model after a handback, from 1 to 600. |
| `seat_retry_s` | whole number | no | `60` | >= 1, <= 3600 | Wall seconds between joins while another client holds the seat, from 1 to 3600. |
| `recall_episodes` | whole number | no | `8` | >= 0, <= 8 | How many episode lines of memory a consult shows, from 0 to 8. |
| `greet_cooldown_s` | whole number | no | `1800` | >= 0, <= 86400 | World seconds before the same person may trigger a greeting again, from 0 to 86400. |
| `horizon_minutes` | whole number | no | `60` | >= 15, <= 480 | World minutes before a punctual next part of the day begins at which the seat is first asked to think about it (the `upcoming` trigger), from 15 to 480. |
| `reask_minutes` | whole number | no | `15` | >= 5, <= 120 | World minutes between two `upcoming` asks while the seat has not set out, arrived, or seen the part begin, from 5 to 120. |

## `[memory]`

The `[memory]` table: where seats' memory is stored. Placement never changes what a seat recalls.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sharing` | one of `none`, `home`, `service` | no | `"home"` | none | How the seats of this process store memory. `home`: one file per world instance for all seats, storing each perceived fact once. `none`: one file per seat. `service` is not available yet. Either choice gives every seat exactly the same memory. |
| `page_cache_kib` | whole number | no | `8192` | >= 256, <= 1048576 | The memory file's page cache in KiB, from 256 to 1 048 576 (SQLite `cache_size`). More makes recall faster and uses more RAM. |
| `verify` | one of `off`, `pass`, `every-commit` | no | `"off"` | none | Debug checks on the memory file. `off`: none. `pass`: before each forgetting pass commits. `every-commit`: before every commit. A failed check stops the seat. |

## `[retry]`

The three retry layers of one table: `[retry]`, `[retry.<layer>]` per table.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `transport` | see the description, or unset | no | unset | none | The transport layer (backoff, Retry-After); unset uses the bundled default. |
| `content` | see the description, or unset | no | unset | none | The content layer (invalid answers, re-asked); unset uses the bundled default. |
| `semantic` | see the description, or unset | no | unset | none | The semantic layer (refused proposals, re-planned); unset uses the bundled default. |

## `[breaker]`

The `[breaker]` table: the per-seat circuit breaker. Unset uses the bundled default.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy` | text | yes | none | none | The policy's id, one of the installed policies (for example `exponential-backoff`). |
| `parameters` | table | no | none | none | The policy's parameters. The policy checks them; an unknown one is refused by name. |

## `[fill]`

The `[fill]` table: the operator's settings of the LM controller's fillers, one table per filler
(`ARC-183`). A filler with no table never lists itself.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `publish-notice` | see the description, or unset | no | unset | none | The `[fill.publish-notice]` table: the price clerk's filler. Unset, an LM seat never posts a notice. |

## `[seat_overrides.<name>]`

The `[seat_overrides.<key>]` tables: per-seat controller bounds and retry layers. The name `seat_overrides` is used so that `seats` can name the subset of seats (D-P6b-3).

`<name>` must match the pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$`. One table per backend:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `controller` | table | no | none | none | The `[seat_overrides.<key>.controller]` table: the seat's own bounds. |
| `retry` | table | no | none | none | The `[seat_overrides.<key>.retry.<layer>]` tables: the seat's own retry layers. |

## Top-level keys

Keys written before the first table of the file.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Bounds | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server` | text, or unset | no | unset | none | The protocol address of the server, for example `ws://127.0.0.1:7878/ws`. Required by the LM controller (`python -m mineworld_cognition`); a loopback address is the usual choice. |
| `invite_env` | text | no | `"MINEWORLD_INVITE"` | none | The NAME of the environment variable that holds the server's invite. The invite is read from the environment only; this file never holds it. |
| `nickname` | text | no | `"cognition"` | length >= 1, length <= 32 | The nickname the controller joins with, from 1 to 32 characters. |
| `store` | text, or unset | no | unset | none | The directory of the controller's own state (memory stores, resume secrets, decision logs). A relative path is resolved against this configuration file. It must not be inside a world. |
| `decisions_json` | text, or unset | no | unset | none | The JSON that `mineworld decisions … --json` printed for the world the server runs. A relative path is resolved against this configuration file. |
| `seats` | see the description, or unset | no | unset | none | Optional subset of the `lm` seats in `decisions_json` to join. Every entry must be an `lm` seat of that file; unset joins all of them. |

## Examples

Each example is a whole file. The test suite loads every block below with the loader.

### A local model

```toml
[recording]
mode = "live"

[tiers]
social = "local"

[backends.local]
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
model = "qwen3.5:4b"
reasoning = "off"
```

### A hosted provider, a budget and a key file

```toml
[recording]
mode = "live"

[tiers]
social = "deepseek"

[budgets]
calls_per_wall_hour = 20
tokens_per_wall_day = 30000
ledger = "cognition-state/budget.sqlite"

[secrets]
env_file = "mineworld.env"

[backends.deepseek]
preset = "deepseek"
model = "your-model-name"
```

### Claude, through an API key

```toml
[recording]
mode = "live"

[tiers]
social = "claude"

[backends.claude]
kind = "anthropic"
base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com"
model = "your-model-name"
key_env = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

### Replay a recording, with no network

```toml
[recording]
mode = "replay"
cassette = "cassettes/recorded.jsonl"

[tiers]
social = "local"

[backends.local]
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
model = "qwen3.5:4b"
```

### Keep one memory file per seat

```toml
[recording]
mode = "replay"
cassette = "cassettes/recorded.jsonl"

[tiers]
social = "local"

[backends.local]
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
model = "qwen3.5:4b"

[memory]
sharing = "none"
```
